symptom: PC0 and PC1 are on the same IP subnet (192.168.50.0/24) but cannot ping each other. Ping from PC0 to PC1 fails with 100% packet loss. No router between them - both are plugged into the same Layer 2 switch.
topology: PC0 connected to Switch0 FastEthernet0/10. PC1 connected to Switch0 FastEthernet0/11. Both PCs are in the 192.168.50.0/24 IP network and should be in the same Layer 2 broadcast domain. Switch0 has two VLANs configured: VLAN 1 (default) and VLAN 50 (ENGINEERING).
show_command_evidence:
[ACTUAL PACKET TRACER EVIDENCE - Collected from real Cisco Packet Tracer scenario by student]

Topology:
PC0 is connected to Switch0 FastEthernet0/10.
PC1 is connected to Switch0 FastEthernet0/11.

Both PCs are configured in the same IP network:
PC0: 192.168.50.10 / 255.255.255.0
PC1: 192.168.50.11 / 255.255.255.0

PC0> ping 192.168.50.11

Packets: Sent = 4, Received = 0, Lost = 4 (100% loss)

Switch0# show vlan brief

VLAN 1   default      active
VLAN 50  ENGINEERING  active

Switch0# show interfaces fastEthernet 0/10 switchport
Access Mode VLAN: 50 (ENGINEERING)

Switch0# show interfaces fastEthernet 0/11 switchport
Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)

Root cause:
The two PCs are in the same IP subnet but their switch ports are assigned to different VLANs. Fa0/10 is in VLAN 50 while Fa0/11 is in VLAN 1, so Layer 2 communication between them fails.

Correct fix:
Assign both intended access ports to the same VLAN, then verify connectivity using ping.

[/ACTUAL PACKET TRACER EVIDENCE]
expected_fault: Switch ports assigned to different VLANs (Fa0/10 in VLAN 50, Fa0/11 in VLAN 1) even though both PCs are in the same IP subnet - VLAN assignment mismatch
expected_fix:
Assign both access ports to the same VLAN on Switch0. Example - to place both PCs in VLAN 50 (ENGINEERING):
  enable
  configure terminal
  interface FastEthernet0/11
   switchport mode access
   switchport access vlan 50
   exit
  end
  write memory
Verify with 'show vlan brief' that both Fa0/10 and Fa0/11 appear under VLAN 50, then run ping 192.168.50.11 from PC0 - should succeed.
